title: Rasheed Walker introductory press conference | Carolina Panthers
text: Hi, >> greetings Rasheed. Can you hear me? >> Yes, I can hear you. >> Hey, good. Uh, I appreciate you taking your time and doing this for us. >> Oh, no problem. Thanks for having me on. >> Yeah. Um, you were the top free agent tackle and you signed um a team friendly contract. You know, I realize every year is a prove it year for NFL players, but are you looking at this opportunity to get a long-term commitment from either the Panthers or another team uh next off season? Um, I think it's just a great opportunity just to play ball, you know. Um, this is my fifth year in the NFL. A lot of guys don't make it to their second contract. So, I'm just happy to be healthy and able to still do the thing I love to do, which is play football. So, >> uh, the Panthers uh, uh, 16 to 13 win uh, was big for the team at the time. uh what was your perception of the Panthers following that game and did it play a role in deciding to to uh to come to Charlotte? >> Um well I think during that game I think Carolina played some complimentary football. Um you know it was a good game. You know we were you know neck and neck for a minute but I mean shoot uh I I don't know like I wouldn't say that had you know something to do with me picking Carolina. I just saw the opportunity and you know I like where the the program was headed and you know I just wanted to be a part of it so that's why I chose Carolina. >> Right. Thanks. Uh good luck. >> Thank you. >> We'll go with David Newton followed by Alex Zitlo. >> Hey Rasheed. David Newton ESPN.com. Appreciate you doing this today. >> Yes sir. >> Wanted to ask you uh back kind of following up on that. Um you had not resigned with Green Bay at the point obviously. Uh, were they How How would you gauge their interest? And then I'll ask a followup to that. >> Um, I mean, I really didn't have like I let my agents take care of, you know, all the talking to the teams and stuff. I just really like, you know, I went into free agency just with a mindset like I was I was just happy to be healthy. You know what I'm saying? Health is well. So, you know, there'll really be a better question for my agent cuz I really didn't ask too many questions. I was just waiting around and you know waiting for the opportunity. >> Well, part of that is cuz the Panthers GM and others have said that they found that the free agents like yourself, top free agents, um seem to be easier to to bring in and get a seat at the table this year than they were a few years ago when the team, you know, was was struggling. Um, how much did that factor in to you and what you saw in Carolina versus maybe two years ago when they were, you know, winning just a handful of games? >> Um, I mean, I feel like my job, you know, as a left tackle is, you know, you know, protect the quarterback, you know, and I feel like, you know, with me coming on to the team, I'm going to make sure I do my job. And with the season that Carolina had last year, um, in addition to me, I feel like I'm gonna make the team better. >> Did they pretty much make you feel that that that wouldn't be back this year or wouldn't be back for most of the year or what was the kind of the conversation like? >> Um, well, everyone, you know, was aware of the situation. I mean, so at the end of the day, like, you know, my good friend Icky is down, but you know, someone has to do the job. And um, you know, I think I'm a very good football player and I think I'm going to help this team get better. >> Appreciate it. >> Hey Rasheed, congrats on the contract and welcome to Charlotte. >> Thank you. Thank you. >> Yeah. Um, I I wanted to follow up on something you just said. Uh, you said my good friend Icky. Uh, how well do you know Icky and how did that relationship start? >> Um, well, we're we're in the same I think we're in the same draft class. Um, I like I liked his game in college. Like I like his college highlights, but um, you know, we've crossed paths plenty of times. You know, we both know who each other are. So, you know, he's cool people. You know, we've talked ever since the signing. And you know, I I was asking about Caroline, asking about the team. Um, he's in high spirits, but yeah, he's he's a really good guy and a great person and an even better football player. >> What about his game did you like? >> Well, no, on his college take when he was at NC State, he was just played just like he had one of the nastiest highlights I ever seen as an offensive lineman. So, you know, that's, you know, that's that's kind of how I got on. And you mentioned that um you and him talked while you were making the decision to ultimately come to Carolina. I'm curious what did he say to you and then ultimately why do you think the Panthers were a good fit for you? >> Well, I talked to him after I signed and I was just asking him, you know, I general questions like where should I live at? Like um you know, how's everything out there? Like how does he like living out there and stuff like that, you know, just stuff regular questions like that. >> Okay. But then from a Panthers fit perspective, like why are the Panthers ideal for you? >> Um, I think the Panthers are ideal for me. Well, honestly, I feel like, you know, I'm the type of person any situation I get, I'm going to make the best of it. So, I feel like that's already a positive. And, you know, I feel like we have a really good quarterback. Bryce Young have I have some good um interior guard help with me. And I feel like my job as a left tackle, I'm going to bring that mindset that, you know, I feel like the team needs to get us over this over the edge. >> Got it. Thanks, man. >> Darren Gant, >> how you doing, Rasheed? Wanted to ask you, you just mentioned those guards. How much do you know about Rob and Damen and and even on the other side of Taylor Motton, having a bunch of veterans on that line with you? >> Well, yeah. I've actually I've met Taylor Motton um once. He's a pretty cool guy. Um, you know, I like his game. Um, Robert Hunt, I saw him catch a pass a couple years ago. Um, that was interesting, but I never met him him or Damian, but I'm looking forward to meeting those guys. But, uh, I'm just ready to get in and start building, you know, building the program, you know, building the franchise up. And, you know what I'm saying? Like the last three out of the four seasons I was at Green Bay, we went to the playoffs. So, you know, I I think I know what it takes to, you know, make it through the playoffs and winning the playoffs. And, you know, with the group of guys that we have and and what the team is building, I feel like, I mean, we have a shot. >> Yeah. What What kind of things are you focused on coming in just in terms of getting to know Rob, Damian, Teemo, and those guys? >> Um, I'm I'm excited to just working with them, you know? Like I mean I feel like offensive line is just you know it's all it is is five guys with the same mindset. So you know I definitely want to get in you know you know break bread with the guys you know get to know them and work with them you know so we can all start playing like as one cohesive unit and all be on the same page. >> Bashtai followed by David Newton. >> Hi Rasheed. Uh welcome to Carolina. I just want to ask you about Bryce Young. What are your thoughts on Bryce Young? And um how have you seen his game evolve from afar as a player in the league? >> Um well, I think Bryce Young, he's a great player. I mean, he text me when I signed. He said, "What's up?" He showed some love. Um I've been watching some of his highlights. I mean, he's just a good player, great athlete. You know, I love when my quarterback is athlete. You know, that's always good. Um but I'm I'mma protect him. I'mma do my job and I'mma, you know, protect them. >> It seems like a few of the guys reached out to you. Is that is that standard or is this kind of are you getting more love than maybe you've gotten in the past from these guys? >> Well, yeah, I really appreciated um um a couple of the guys reaching out to me. It definitely made me feel like I was entering into like, you know, a home environment. Uh this this I mean this is my only team I've ever played with on the Packers. you know, when I came in, guys like Aaron Jones and Kenny Clark greeted me with open arms. So, it felt good to have the same, you know, greetings and, you know, for my new teammates to show me some love. >> Thanks, >> David. You muted yourself. >> David, you're still on mute. >> Sorry about that. house. Uh, can you tell me how you think the the gun charge you had might have impacted free agency for you? >> Um, you know, I mean that's going to be that's getting dismissed, but any questions you have to um talk to my lawyer? >> Okay. Can you tell us your version of what happened there? >> No, I don't want to talk about that. >> All right. Thank you. >> Any more questions? >> Yeah. Yeah, I have a couple. I'm sorry. Sorry, I'm on my in my car and couldn't figure out the raise hand thing. Can Can you hear me? >> Yeah, go ahead, Joe. >> Okay. Hey, thanks, Kia. And uh thanks, Rasheed. Um there was there was a report that maybe some teams got scared off by your medicals. Did Did one, were you surprised that your market wasn't more robust? I I know a lot of folks thought, you know, you you were going to get a multi-year deal for a lot of money. And then secondly, you know, did did that get back to you or your agent that you know that folks had some medical questions? >> Um, I don't know. I mean, like I said, I was just sitting around waiting. You know, I did my four years at Green Bay and I was just happy I got another opportunity to play somewhere else. And I feel like, you know, wherever I landed at, they were getting a steal anyway because what I bring to a team is, you know, I bring intensity. Um the the I'm a great teammate. I work hard and I go hard for my teammates. So, you know what I'm saying? I feel like, you know, by the grace of God, I landed in Carolina. I feel like it's going to be a great fit and I'm just ready ready to do my job. >> Completely understand that. That's uh and you saying you feel like you're a steal. And it kind of gets back to an earlier question, but do you feel like you go do your thing this year, then, you know, you you get to do this free agency thing uh again next year and and hopefully uh it's more beneficial for you? >> Um I feel like it's it's always going to be bene I'm I'm always going to be in a you know, beneficial situation as long as I'm healthy because I'm always going to do what I'm supposed to do and I'm a good football player.

title: Tyler Shough & Taliese Fuaga press conference Q&A | Saints in France
text: You've been in Paris for a few days now. How do you like your new home city? I can give you an American answer and a French answer. The American answer would be this is the greatest city in the world. This is the best place ever. And the French answer would be pas mal. Pas mal. I know New Orleans is one of the finest city in the US when it comes to food, but did you have some time to enjoy French cuisine? I didn't know how to use the utensils at first and they had to show me. So, I felt very American and I'm sorry, but it was a it was fantastic. Um I think it we're excited to have some food here tonight, but it's you can't be here long enough. We got to we're so excited to come back. Did you ever imagine that you would be running out to play American football in a stadium in Paris in your career, Taysom? Um no. I mean uh it's kind of crazy cuz you see uh many international players like uh Dembélé. Um Many guys on PSG. I mean, all over. It's kind of crazy seeing those guys playing on that field and just being able to be on that field it's a it's a blessing for us. It was amazing. It was amazing. I think it was the The thing I like the most about it was I think there's not a bad seat in the in the stadium. It's very very circular. Reminds us of the dome. Um just has the open open top which we love. So, um what an honor. I think the coolest part we were talking about is just coming from America and it's it seems so far away to come here and now being around the people, being around the culture. Um it feels like a new home and then we want to go out here and represent. Uh guys, how important is it to Mrs. Benson and to the Saints uh to make history here in the fall? Do Do you feel like you will be part of history? I think it's very important. I think that's why she's made it her mission and and the New Orleans Saints, the entire organization. We feel that that bond and connection and um we want to represent you all. We want to represent the people of France. Um that's the best part about Louisiana in my opinion is the people and the culture and and how strongly we protect our own and and we're obviously not from there, but we've they've kind of adopted us and and Miss Benson um in particular. So, we want to represent you all and and go out there and and win. Guys, it will be some people's first interaction with American football in France. That That will be the first time they see American football with you guys. What does it feel like to be an ambassador, Taysom? It's crazy cuz uh you know, I didn't think I'd get this far in football, but just being here just to uh kind of express the American football here is uh it's good feeling cuz uh you see a lot of kids out here playing flag football and everything, but you know, hopefully we can uh you know, get American football more bigger out here. So, it'll be fun. Yeah, you see the you see the passion about football here in France and you see the passion about American football as well. And I think we have that passion that we've grown up as kids and and learned it in America and uh we want to bring that here. We want to bring that everywhere as far as just the um watching American football game is a it's a feeling like no other and it's comparable to football here. So, it's um we're we're just excited and thankful to even be here cuz we we feel very undeserving and we feel um very honored um more than anything. Taysom, Taylor, you're obviously the quarterback your first season How excited are you for next season? Uh I'm fired up. I can't wait. We've been Ty and I have been training every single day. We've been working out. Um we're just itching to play again. I think you see the vision of the front office. You see the vision of coach Kellen Moore um of Gayle Benson and and I think everybody's on the same page and we want to we want to go out there and win it all and do everything that we can. I think that we know we can do a lot of things in this league right now. First thing we just got to win the division, but you know, uh I think we're we're coming up right now. So. Do you have a message uh for budding French players who want to make it in the NFL? You know, just keep going. Follow your dreams. There's nothing that can hold you back as long as you believe you can do it. Cuz your period mostly in the shadow, your job is basically to protect Taysom from the opponent. What makes a good offensive lineman like you? Um I think a big thing is just communication. You know, uh there's five of us that are trying to protect this guy and we have to be in uh the same same uh you know, uh wavelength and everything with it, you know, so if we're not on the same page, we can't protect this guy, but you know, he's the the big arm and everything. We got to get him going. So. Communication, a bit of working out, too? Yeah, a bit of working out, yeah. Got to stay off the food, huh? So, Taylor, how much do you like these guys, the offensive lineman? I suppose you are always nice to them. Got We got to. We go to eat We go to dinner every Thursday. Um and that's the best part about New Orleans and now and now France is we find a new restaurant to go eat and just break bread and have fun and um they're the best guys on the team because he's being humble, but he's 300 and 30 lb. How old is he? I mean, 315? I don't know. He's 300 plus lb, but he can run 20 mph and he he can jump and he's the the most athletic people on the field and that's why they're the most important. So, um obviously my role is is is spread out um and and there's a lot of direction and obviously passing the ball to the other guys um on the field and um it's a great great honor though. It's And that's the best part why we love American football. We feel like it's the one of the best team sports is because it takes everybody. Taylor, everybody in the world knows what a quarterback is thanks to TV, films, Netflix, the the series quarterbacks, but can you describe how difficult this position is and how much information you need to process in real time? Um yeah, it's it's it's incredibly difficult, but that's why you love it. And I think the biggest thing is you have the ball in your hands every single play and more than anything you have to know what everybody else is doing on the field on on your offense and you also all have to know what the entire defense is doing and their job is to throw you off and try and disguise and um there's 100 plus different plays in you know, different formations or set pieces in soccer and there's 100 plus different formations and then that we can get into at any certain point of time. So, um the biggest part is the mental like he was talking about. You see the physicality of of football, but more than anything it's the the mental side. Any personal goals for this season, guys? I think we we got to win the division. I think it starts with We have it We have team success um and that leads to individual success. Um we want to win the division. We want to win the Super Bowl. And and then after that, that's where all the fun things happen. And so, that's that's our main goal. Um like you said, winning the division. Uh starts with one game at a time, but we're trying to win in the locker room first, you know, if we can't beat each other up at practice first, then we can't win the games out there. So. Uh on a last note, guys, you guys are being ambassadors of your sport and your team. Why should all French people now be Saints fan? I'll let you I'll give you the floor to give your arguments. Well, other than the the obvious connection of the the French Louisiana connection, but we got the most We have the most fun. We have the most swag. We got a young team. We got a bunch of a young young and up-and-coming guys. We want to have fun. We want to bring energy to the field. The black and gold, you can't miss it. You got the We got the best swag, the best gear. Um and we and we want to go out there and win. We got to go out there and we want to represent you all more than anything. I think that's the best part about Louisiana like I said is the passion. So, we want to bring that here. Uh the community out there, man. You know, you got stuff like Mardi Gras and stuff like you know, you want to party all that? Just come over, man. It's it's a it's a fun experience and everything. So, just come out there and we'll we'll we'll take care of you guys. Yeah. And we'll finish on that. Thank you so much, guys.

title: Post-Signing 1-on-1: LB Leo Chenal | Free Agency Friday x Next Man Up | Washington Commanders
text: Commanders family, welcome in a free agency Fridays. We are here in the Big Bear AI Command Center studio for a special version of next man up because we got one of our new linebackers in the building. Leo Chanel just pulled up, just put pen to paper. You got your bag, man. How you feeling? I'm feeling great. Being here already, man, I feel the energy, the love of the game just like it's seeping through. You know, every everybody staff top to bottom, few players walking everybody's just like ready to go, man. The culture is is awesome and welcoming here. Congratulations, man. We're so happy to have you be here and you were a highly sought after free agent. What makes you say you're I'm going to leave the Chiefs? You've been there for your whole career. What makes you say you want to come in? Yeah, I mean, not going to lie, it was tough. You know, that was that was my team. I never really saw myself leaving there and, you know, just became a reality and, you know, you guys came came over and just talking with coach Quinn, coach Jones and just hearing so much about them and what they bring to the table, hearing that all the guys love them. You know, even peers to them, everybody has just so much respect for them and just knowing the players, the guys they got on this team already and we didn't meet expectations last year here, but, you know, I just know the culture, the guys that we have in this building, guys we're bringing in. We got some dudes who are making making runs in free agency like, you name it. We're about to be have a great draft, you know it. So, I'm just excited to be part of it. I'm loving that we. We we we. I love it all of that stuff, man. And this was we talked about it before we started recording. This is your first free agency period where you've got to be sought after, where you had to go through this. What was it like, man? Because I understand that that could be a little stressful. Yeah, I mean, it's different. You know, draft is like, okay, you're going here whether you like it or not and now it's, you know, I got some options. I get to choose, you know, what best fits me and I got to look for my family, look out for my family as well, my girls. So, it's cool being able to, okay, like what do I like? What culture, you know, fits me best? What what way will they utilize me? You know, how are the you know, the coaches whatever it is, you know, I can I can specifically point that out and and and choose for myself and you know, again, it was it was kind of an easy decision, you know, being here, ready to raise hell. So, ready to go. [laughter] We love that, man. When you talk about those conversations you did have, and they're talking about how they're going to use you and utilize you, what were some of those conversations like? It's just, you know, having having that experience, you know, in in KC and Wisconsin whether I can be in the middle of the field off the ball, a weakside linebacker, whether I need to be on the ball, you know, addressing the tackle, whatever it is. You know, I can do it. You know, and and they were very encouraging and welcoming in that fact and that's kind of what made made it very attractive. Just the way they were excited to, you know, take advantage of my skill set, you know, my athleticism and just really looking forward to it. >> And that versatility is shown on the film, right? You've been all over the field. Where are you most comfortable at? You know, I I have definitely most reps, you know, off the ball and I want to continue to grow on the ball if I can as a pass rusher. You know, it's great learning from guys Chris Jones, George Karlaftis, Charles Charles we got Charles Menahu Chuck, you know, over here. So, they were great mentors to me. You know, they love the game and so I want to keep building especially on the ball pass rush. You know, cuz I've done, you know, middle of the field off the ball, you know, rushing on guards, rushing on running backs and that's where I definitely excel. So, it's continue to build that and continue to make plays in the in the pass game as well. And you really fit the bill for what we've heard from our new defensive coordinator Dorante Jones on what he wants. He wants versatility. He wanted us to get younger. He wanted us to get faster and you showed that athleticism on tape years ago. Let's check it out real quick. >> Oh, here we go. Look at that man right there. Now, I looked it up, my brother. 15 ft on average. That's how big a double decker bus is on average, 15 ft. And you just jump up there and you climb up there and get this had Commanders fans so excited that they had a freak athlete that was capable of just pulling up something like this. What's going on in this video, man? >> What's going on? If you really want to know, [laughter] it's a parade. So, it's you know, a little something in the system, to be honest with you. >> [laughter] >> You know, I was just hyped up. You know, you win something like that, you get excited. And to be honest, actually, like my wife, you know, she was pregnant at the time. She was up there. You know, she's getting like champagne sprayed in her face and I'm like, oh shoot, I'm out in the street. I got my wife up here still. So, I remembered her. So, I'm like, oh shoot, what's the fastest way to get down this bus? I'm like, [laughter] I I got to try to jump, you know. Like the bus I think was the bus moving? Maybe? It looked like it it looked like it might have had a little bit of Okay, it was still. It was still. >> Okay, so I was I was being a little safe, you know. Still impressive. Yeah, so. No, I I had to get up there quick, you know. A hormonal wife is >> I understand. I got to get in trouble. I got to I'm going to get on this bus right now. How did you end up off the bus? Why weren't you on the bus to begin with? You go down, you know, they they have you go down if you want to be up there, you know, you got cigars and, you know, wherever you want to hang out with your family up top. But if you want to be crazy like Willie Gay, you know, he's Willie Gay all-time teammate Willie Gay. He's awesome. >> He was on the street, you know, high-fiving fans. Such such a cool thing to be part of. We'll experience that that shortly, I hope. Oh, yeah. And, you know, just just a lot of stuff going through. Adrenaline, you name it. Now, we normally don't show videos on next man up, but to me when I watch that, that shows why Commanders fans are so excited to have you. That's an athletic freak right there. That's a bad man. Believe it or not, that is an athletic freak and that's what we have seen on the film. When you talk to Dorante Jones, our new defensive coordinator, how excited are you to play for a guy like that that knows how to utilize somebody with all your different skill sets? Oh, former former Wisconsin Badger. That's that's that's the biggest part right there. But no, I mean, you know, what he brought to the table, you know, what utilized, you know, Minnesota, whatever it is, like he knew how to get guys involved. You know, a lot of times, you know, you get you get defensive line, you know, eating and, you know, enjoying the benefit. They work really hard, you know, you got to have that and so it's it's cool also, you know, have linebackers involved, too. You know, and not speak not speaking ill of anywhere else and they do great job at KC, but, you know, just speaking to me personally, what I what I can bring to the table, you know, individually to be able to help this team out is is pretty cool just hearing it. At this point in your career, do you feel like you've been underutilized a little bit? You know, it's it happens, you know. I love, you know, everything we had going on in KC and it just happens, you know, with the business and, you know, whatever it is, but I feel like I can be utilized definitely more now and be able to have that [snorts] role, you know, whatever whatever the reason may be. Like I'm just excited to be part of it. >> Yeah, do you have like that hunger to be that every down linebacker? Like I mean, I got to imagine so, right? >> Yeah, I mean, that's that's what made it a lot easier, you know, leaving there, coming here. Just speaking the opportunity, what I can do, what I can bring to the table, be on be on the field as much as I want to and as much as I can with whatever the coaches want ask of me. So, I'm just I'm really excited for the opportunity. And then we watched that video and of course you're celebrating a Super Bowl. You got two of them things, man, and I know that that is the Mecca of all things, right? Getting that Super Bowl. How can you help take what you've learned from those Super Bowl appearances, what you've learned from playing in those Super Bowl locker rooms? How can you take that here and help these young guys out? Yeah, I'm used to, you know, we have a long season already, but I'm used to, you know, going late into February, having the first game of the season. So, I'm I'm used to those things. I'm used to being in the big moments, the most high-stakes, high-pressure situations and knowing how to be level-headed. You know, sometimes it's everybody loves the game of football. Everybody's juiced up, ready to play. They want to hit somebody. They want to catch a ball in the end zone. But the biggest guys know how to balance it, you know, and balance the the focus and the energy. So, I think just having that experience going to three Super Bowls really helped me have that that balance cuz, you know, like I said, it's easy to get get revved up in the in those situations. So, I could bring that experience as well, you know, cuz playoff football Super Bowl Super Bowl football is a lot different than regular season games. So, I'm ready, you know, with that experience. And it takes a certain type of team, right? It takes a certain type of locker room. A lot of things have to go right to win a Super Bowl. When you look at what we have here currently, right? There's a lot of new faces including you. But when you look at what we have here currently with the Commanders, do you see Super Bowl hopes there? >> really do. You know, just the culture alone, you know, that's that's a big thing. Like you look around like, how are the guys responding to things? How are how are guys walking in the locker room like every single day and it makes it makes a big difference, you know, and uh just seeing these guys already, you know, they they got it. You know, I can see it, you know, in the coaches' eyes, you know, the players that I met so far in their eyes, their excitement, the way they talk. You know, they were you know, they I've seen like how they play on film. Obviously, again, we didn't meet expectations last year, but I know that we're capable of it, you know, what they've showed you know, before that and you know, what these players are capable of, the guys they're bringing in, like the you know, those dudes, man, they're ballers we're bringing in. Like I said, we're going to have a great draft. We're going to have the team, the players to do it. We're going to have the energy, the culture, like you name it. It's it's just up to us how we utilize it. Talk about those guys they're bringing in. There's another Chief coming in the building, man. How was it? How was it? Have you guys had those conversations knowing that you guys will both be here? >> Yeah, as soon as soon as I saw the the notification, you know, he's coming. I'm like, I I reached out to him. I'm like, dude, let's go. Like that's the best feeling, you know, just got you to coming in coming in together and, you know, I love Chuck. You know, he's a great dude. He's hungry, like hungrier than anybody. You know, you can put him up there and he's he's been with the systems. I know how to get to the ball. He's been with San Fran, whatever and he he just knows. He's a great vet with great knowledge and I'm joining up with Allegretti, Wylie as well and a coach Jones, a little Wisconsin connection. So, it's nice having that familiarity, too, and and also look forward to building new relationships. Leo, welcome home, man. And finally, in closing, man, the fans are so excited to hear from you. That's your ISO cam right there, man. Can you just give the fans a message on what to expect from Leo Chanel now that he's in the building? >> Yeah, you know, I'm ready to just bring violence, physicality. I've mentioned it before.
